EDI Base

The common ground of every EDI and Peppol connection — the EDI message log, its states, sending and receiving, and the partner settings all providers share.

Version19.0.1.9.1
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresaccount, account_add_gln
Extended byedi_base_gs1, edi_base_peppol, edi_base_purchase, edi_base_queue_job, edi_base_sale, edi_editel_base, edi_epostak_base, edi_grit_base

What it is for

Every electronic document Odoo exchanges with a trading partner through an EDI provider — an order, an order response, a despatch advice, an invoice, a Peppol e-invoice or a business response — is recorded as one EDI message. This module provides that log and the machinery around it:

  • the EDI → Messages list, where every inbound and outbound document of every provider is kept with its raw XML;
  • the states a message passes through and the buttons that move it on;
  • how an outbound message is handed to the provider and how inbound documents are collected, stored and processed;
  • the GLN of every contact and a per-customer switch for automatic sending.

On its own it connects to nothing. A provider module does the transport:

Provider Modules
Editel (eXite) edi_editel_*
GRiT (Orion) edi_grit_*
ePošťák (Peppol access point) edi_epostak_peppol

What happens to orders, deliveries and invoices is described in the guides for the sales side, edi_base_sale, the purchase side, edi_base_purchase, and Peppol e-invoicing, edi_base_peppol.

Setting it up

  1. Give people access. The EDI menu is visible only to members of two groups, set on the user (Settings → Users):
Group Can
EDI User see the EDI menu, the messages and the EDI tabs on documents
EDI Manager everything above, plus Send, Reprocess and creating or changing messages

An administrator is not in either group by default; add yourself first. Sending a Peppol invoice creates an EDI message, so whoever sends one needs EDI Manager (see Peppol e-invoicing). 2. Record your own GLN on your company's contact (field GLN, tab Sales & Purchase), and the GLN of every EDIFACT trading partner. Peppol connections identify parties by their Peppol address instead — see the Peppol guide. 3. Install and configure the provider. Its settings appear in Settings → EDI, or from EDI → Configuration → Settings (system administrators only).

Contacts

On the contact form, tab Sales & Purchase:

Field What it does
GLN The contact's Global Location Number. Odoo shows it only on delivery addresses; here it is shown on every contact, because any EDI party — your company, the customer, the invoicee, the delivery point — is identified by it. Contacts can be searched by GLN.
Override EDI auto-send Off (default): outbound EDI messages for this customer or vendor follow the provider's global auto-send settings. On: the provider modules show per-document choices (always / never / default) that take precedence for this company and all its contacts.

Two more fields belong to the EDIFACT providers and are described below.

The message log

EDI → Messages lists every message, newest first. Red rows are in error, orange rows carry a warning or come from a test environment, grey rows are done. Filters: Inbound, Outbound, Test Mode, Production, Errors, Pending (draft, ready or received), Done, Peppol BIS3; grouping by provider, message type, direction, state or partner.

The message form shows:

Field Meaning
Document Name the file name of the document
Provider the transport (Editel, GRiT, ePošťák, …)
Document Family EDIFACT or Peppol BIS3 — the document standard, independent of the provider
Message Type ORDERS, ORDRSP, DESADV, INVOIC, … for EDIFACT; Invoice, CreditNote, MLR, InvoiceResponse for Peppol
Direction Inbound / Outbound
Environment the provider's test or production mode, stamped when the message was created; a test message carries a TEST ribbon
Partner resolved from the sender's (inbound) or receiver's (outbound) GLN or Peppol address
Message ID, Message Date, Sender GLN, Receiver GLN read from the document itself; for Peppol, the "GLN" fields hold the Peppol endpoints
External Reference, Customer / Vendor Reference your document number and the counterparty's order number, so one conversation (order → response → despatch → invoice) can be searched by one reference
Provider Interchange ID, Transmission UUID the provider's own identifiers — quote them to the provider's support
Error Details, Blocking Level why the message failed, and whether it is a warning or an error
XML Content the document, indented for reading

The XML is always stored as an attachment of the message; documents up to 1 MB are also shown inline. Links to the order, delivery, invoice or bill the message belongs to are added by the sale, purchase and Peppol modules, which also put an EDI Messages tab on those documents.

A message belongs to the company of the document it was created for, not to the company the user happened to be working in, and it is sent and processed as that company.

States

State Outbound Inbound
Draft created, not yet prepared —
Ready generated and waiting to be sent (automatic sending off, or waiting for you) —
Queued handed over for sending, not yet accepted by the provider —
Sent accepted by the provider —
Received — stored, waiting to be processed or being reprocessed
Error sending failed; see Error Details processing failed; the document is kept
Done finished: for some providers this means delivery to the recipient was confirmed (see the provider's guide) processed: the order, bill or response was created or recorded

What Sent and Done prove differs by provider. For ePošťák, Sent means the access point accepted the document for transport and only Done means the recipient's access point received it — see delivery status.

Sending

Provider modules create outbound messages from documents — automatically when a document is confirmed or posted, if automatic sending is on, or when you press the provider's send button. To send or re-send a message yourself:

  • Send on the message form (EDI Manager), for outbound messages in Draft, Ready, Queued or Error;
  • several at once: select them in the list, Actions → Send (queue dispatch). A dialog lists what will be sent and what will be skipped (inbound messages, messages already sent or done) before anything happens.

Sending clears the previous error, moves the message to Queued and writes a line on the order, delivery or invoice it belongs to ("… queued for dispatch via …").

How a queued message leaves

Each provider declares one of two ways:

  • Job queue. The message becomes a background job of the OCA job runner (queue_job), linked to the message by edi_base_queue_job. The Editel and GRiT connectors work this way and install it. A message with jobs shows a Queue Jobs button; on the job, the Related button opens the message, and the job list can be filtered by message. A job is attempted up to five times.
  • Scheduled action. EDI: send queued messages (no job runner) runs every 2 minutes and sends up to 100 queued messages of the providers registered for it — ePošťák is one. Each message is sent on its own: a temporary failure (the provider unavailable, a rate limit) leaves it Queued with a warning in Error Details and a Retry Not Before: the provider's own Retry-After, else a pause that doubles with each attempt (2, 4, 8 … minutes, at most an hour). After five temporary failures — a rate limit does not count as one — it moves to Error with the last reason; so does any other failure at once. Sending it again starts the count afresh. One unsendable message does not stop or undo the others, and each message's outcome is saved before the next is sent, so a run that is interrupted keeps what the provider already accepted. When the run's time is up, the rest stay queued for the next run.

The choice is the provider's, not the database's, so a database with both never sends one message twice.

Receiving

Each provider has its own scheduled action that collects new documents. For every document:

  1. If a message with the same message ID from the same provider was already received, the document is skipped as a duplicate (and acknowledged). A provider family can make this stricter: for Peppol the sender, the receiver and the document kind must match as well — see receiving Peppol documents.
  2. Otherwise it is stored first, with its XML, as a message in Received.
  3. It is then processed — an order, a bill, a response is created or recorded — and the message moves to Done. If processing fails, the message moves to Error with the reason in Error Details; the document is not lost.
  4. The document is acknowledged to the provider, so it is not delivered again.

When the provider reports that more documents are waiting, the collection runs again at once instead of waiting for the next interval.

Reprocess (EDI Manager, inbound messages in Received or Error) runs step 3 again — typically after you have created a missing product or recorded a contact's GLN.

Matching products

Inbound order and delivery lines are matched to products in this order:

  1. the barcode — tried as sent, without leading zeros, and padded to 8, 12, 13 and 14 digits, because partners disagree on padding EAN codes;
  2. the sender's own code for the product (Vendor Product Code on the product's vendor line), if the sender is known;
  3. the product's internal reference.

If a line matches nothing, the whole incoming order fails by default and the error lists every unmatched line (EAN, quantity, price, names and codes) with the advice to create the products and reprocess. edi_base_sale_pending changes that, see pending lines.

Variable symbol

Where a message carries a variable symbol — the supplier's bank details in an outbound INVOIC, the paid bill in a REMADV — it is the symbol a Czech or Slovak payment order uses: digits only, at most ten. It is the Variable Symbol from l10n_cssk_payment_symbols when that is installed; otherwise the digits of the Payment Reference, else of the invoice number (on a vendor bill, of the supplier's number), keeping the last ten. INV/2026/00012 becomes 202600012. When there are no digits at all the element is left out.

EDIFACT party identity (GS1)

edi_base_gs1, installed with the Editel and GRiT providers, adds the GS1 party settings EDIFACT exchanges need and Peppol does not:

Where Field Meaning
Contact EDI Communication Endpoint The contact whose GLN owns the EDI mailbox, used as sender/recipient of the envelope while the buyer, invoicee and delivery place keep their own GLNs. Set it on the company; its contacts inherit it. Empty: the contact's own GLN.
Contact EDI DESADV in SSCC mode Despatch advices for this customer use the SSCC package structure instead of a flat list of articles. Set on the company; its contacts inherit it.
Warehouse (form, next to the address) EDI GLN (Delivery Point) The GLN of the warehouse as the delivery place in outbound documents and for matching incoming despatch advices; the company's GLN is used when empty.

Limitations

  • Dates and times in EDIFACT documents are read and written in the time zone of the system parameter edi.timezone (default Europe/Bratislava).
  • For EDIFACT documents, duplicate detection compares the interchange's message ID and the provider only; Peppol adds the sender, the receiver and the document kind (see Peppol limitations).
  • Messages cannot be deleted from the user interface; nobody has delete rights on them.
